## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fd9a7fa743994ae28ba24c0cb4e00feb3b803b4d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md + scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs (the `--template` legend, the `--brief-template` ③ line, the two constants and the self-test pins). Read, not reviewed: scripts/pm/verify-review-tier.mjs, scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs, AGENTS.md (Prime Directive 5), SKILL.md, references/execution-duties.md and references/landing-operations.md on `main`.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Four nits.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Diff shape — right.** One commit on merge-base `bc6b7ffd`; 2 files, +46 −5. contract-review.md +3 −3 (lines 36–38 only). record-recognisers.mjs hunks at 1989 (constants), 2074 (legend), 2302 (brief), 2471 and 2477 (battery floors), 3313 and 3361 (pins).
- **No reader changes — right.** No recogniser, parser or accept set is touched; only printed text grows (legend +5 lines, brief +2 lines, both unconditional across faces). Two new exports, `PUSH_DOWN_CHECK` and `FACELESS_FINDING_CARRIER`, in an internal script.
- **Mailbox region untouched — confirmed.** The mailbox doorbell block starts at line 1247; the nearest hunk is at 1989. `readMailboxComment`, `MAILBOX_KEYS` and `mailboxEvents` are byte-identical to `main`.
- **Ratchet and line budget — right.** The file is 63 lines against the ratchet row of 63. Lines 35–38 measure 118/118/119/118 bytes. The only lines over 120 are 22 and 23, both untouched.
- **Re-flow kept meaning — right.** `贴:` moved up a line; 「调用显式传该档 model」 became 「显式传该档 model」; 「给其输出文件」 became 「给输出文件」. The only meaning changes are the two intended ones: the session route's condition, and 「拒即子代理重跑」 naming where to re-run. No script pins the old wording (grep on the head: none).
- **No issue numbers in operative skill text — right.** The three new lines carry none; the file has no three-digit `#` reference. The printed brief stays under its existing `#digit` pin.
- **Check-runs on the head.** No failure. Success includes `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset` and `Check PR Size`. **Still pending when read (9):** `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`. The ratchet, the id-lint and the recogniser self-test are judged by those runs, not by this record; I did not confirm which job carries each. This PASS is on the contract; the all-green landing check stands on its own.

### ② Semver level

None. No package is touched, so nothing is published. The `skip-changeset` label is on the PR and `Check Changeset` is green. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the PR body and the claim, and both are right for this diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question (carrier in the `--template` legend only) — answered: A, leave it there.** The ③ line of contract-review.md measures exactly 120 bytes, so naming the carrier there buys a line. The rules already give the answer without it: line 18 gives a faceless PR to the seat's self-read, line 44 says the self-read runs the same check, and execution-duties.md makes the ACCEPT verdict a comment on the PR that lists its findings. See N3 for the limit of option A.
- **Dev out-of-scope note** (a card thread that messaged its seat or loaded a skill already fails the session route) — true against the verifier, and it is what the new bullet now says. No card owed.
- **File surface — held.** Both files are the claimed surface; record-recognisers.mjs stays in the template, brief and self-test regions.
- **Author:** the PR is relay-written; no foreign-login note is owed.
- **SQL push-down check:** not applicable. The diff holds no query, id materialisation or join.

### ④ Design judgment

**1. The session-evidence bullet against `verify-review-tier.mjs` (unchanged from `main`).**

What `handsWorkToAnotherAgent` refuses:
- the exact names `Agent`, `Task`, `Workflow`, `SendMessage`;
- `Skill`;
- a connector tool whose name starts with send, message, start, fire, spawn, dispatch, delegate or interrupt, in any casing;
- a connector tool that ends in `_trigger` or `_triggers`;
- a connector tool that names a session, agent, subagent, copilot, thread, trigger or worker under any first word that is not a read verb.

The bullet's three conditions (started no other agent, sent no message, called no Skill) are a true summary of the main doors, and its remedy is right. It is both narrower and wider than the tool:
- **Narrower:** it does not name the fail-closed shapes. A session that only renamed or resolved its own thread, set a session title, created or updated a trigger, resolved a GitHub review thread or requested a copilot review is refused too.
- **Wider:** 「未发消息」 reads as any message. A `post_message` to the user or a GitHub comment does not refuse.

Neither gap can produce a wrong record: the write tool runs the verifier before the write, and the bullet says a refusal means a sub-agent re-run. The cost is one wasted in-seat attempt, or one avoidable sub-agent run.

- N1 (nit) — the three conditions are a summary, not the tool's set. If the line is ever re-flowed, 「未驱动他 agent、线程或会话」 is closer than 「未发消息」.

**2. The push-down wording against the merged check.** On `main` the check lives at contract-review.md line 44 and AGENTS.md Prime Directive 5. `PUSH_DOWN_CHECK` is the English that the landing PR gave that line, word for word: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a finding unless a reason is given. The pointer (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first) is accurate. No paraphrase drift. Every face carries it, the declaration face included, which matches 「恒查」.

- N2 (nit) — the wording exists three times: the constant and two hand-wrapped line arrays. The printed text is not built from the constant; the pins hold the copies together. This works, and it keeps the pin independent of what it pins, but the constant's only consumer is the self-test.
- N4 (nit) — the new legend entry reads as the definition of ③ and omits the foreign-author note that contract-review.md line 43 puts in ③. The brief's ③ line had the same gap before this PR.

**3. The faceless carrier against the ACCEPT rules.** Consistent. execution-duties.md defines the ACCEPT verdict as a PR comment (`## 席位核对`) carrying the checklist result and deviations. SKILL.md has ACCEPT itemise findings one per line, and its pointer form is `ACCEPT → PR #n comment`. landing-operations.md starts after ACCEPT and says nothing against it.

- N3 (nit) — the sentence lives in a legend that a seat self-reading a faceless PR has no reason to open, since no record is owed there. If the carrier ever needs to be in the rules, its home is the ACCEPT line in execution-duties.md, not the ③ line here. The legend also says where the finding goes, not what it does to the verdict; the existing REWORK rule covers that.

**4. The three pins.**
- The legend pin runs over the bare shape and all four faces, and checks the collapsed text holds the check between the ③ and ④ entries.
- The carrier pin compares against a literal sentence and a literal constant value, not a derived one.
- The brief pin slices the fenced region, so it proves the check is inside what gets copied and directly after the ③ line.

They pin the right things. The mutation claim is credible from the structure: deleting either line array or rewording the carrier sentence breaks exactly one pin each. The battery floors (30 to 32, 23 to 24) match two pins placed in the template battery and one in the brief battery. One guard in the legend pin (`EVERY_FACE.length === REVIEW_FACES.length + 1`) is true by construction and asserts nothing.
